title: Given each of the 45 non-permitted (state, event) pairs, dispatch returns RejectedNotPermitted, leaves state() unchanged, and calls no guard
preconditions: For each (start state, event) pair a fresh machine is constructed; allowing fake wired to every GuardId before the start state is forced

inputs: cross product of six states and nine events minus the nine permitted pairs
steps: 1. For each of the six start states and each event not permitted in that state, construct a fresh FlightStateMachine | 2. Wire the allowing fake to GuardId::Arm, GuardId::Recovery, and GuardId::ServiceReset | 3. Force the start state with its permitted path through the public API (BOOT: none; INITIALIZING: ResetCompleted; DISARMED: ResetCompleted, InitPassed; ARMED: DISARMED path then ArmRequest; FAILSAFE: ARMED path then CriticalFaultToFailsafe; FAULT: ResetCompleted, InitFailed) | 4. Reset the fake's call record | 5. Call dispatch(event) once | 6. Read the DispatchResult, state(), and the fake's recorded calls
expected_result: for all 45 pairs: outcome RejectedNotPermitted; row index equals -1; state() equals the start state; fake recorded zero calls

notes: Parent ID for rejection cases; other rejection cases have their own NEW IDs. Pair list is hand-written from SRS 10, not read from the table. No state setter exists, so start states are forced through events. The zero-call assertion is not vacuous: the guard is wired before the start state is forced and the call record is reset after forcing.

title: Given allowing guards on every GuardId, dispatching each of the 54 (state, event) pairs yields Accepted for exactly the 9 permitted pairs, each with a distinct non-negative row index
preconditions: For each pair a fresh machine is forced to the pair's state through the public API; allowing fake wired to every GuardId; the test has no access to kTransitionTable
mocks: IStateGuard (fake): evaluate() returns allowed=true for every call and records each (state, event) argument
inputs: cross product of six states and nine events (54 pairs); hand-written permitted set: (BOOT, ResetCompleted), (INITIALIZING, InitPassed), (INITIALIZING, InitFailed), (DISARMED, ArmRequest), (ARMED, DisarmRequest), (ARMED, CriticalFaultToFailsafe), (ARMED, CriticalFaultToFault), (FAILSAFE, RecoveryAccepted), (FAULT, ServiceReset)
steps: 1. For each pair construct a fresh FlightStateMachine and wire the allowing fake to GuardId::Arm, GuardId::Recovery, and GuardId::ServiceReset | 2. Force the pair's state through its permitted path as in TC-STATE-003 step 3 | 3. Call dispatch(event) once | 4. Record outcome, row, and from of the DispatchResult | 5. After all 54 calls, count the Accepted results and collect their row values
expected_result: outcome Accepted for exactly the 9 permitted pairs and RejectedNotPermitted for the other 45; the 9 Accepted results have pairwise different row values, each 0 or greater; each Accepted from equals the pair's state
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on the Accepted count and per-pair outcome; EXPECT_EQ on the number of distinct row values
notes: Replaces the earlier kTransitionTable inspection: the table is private to flight_state_table.cpp (design 4.1) and no test seam is used. Row count and key uniqueness are observed through the Accepted count and distinct row indices. Specific row index values are not asserted (design defines only -1 for none). Enumerator validity of from and to is guaranteed by enum class typing, so no separate assertion. Overlaps TC-STATE-003 on the rejected side by design.

title: Given a denying guard on each of D4, D8, and D9, dispatch returns RejectedGuardDenied with the guard's reason and the state is unchanged
preconditions: Three independent machines, one per row, each forced to the row's from state through permitted events; guards are wired once at construction and never re-wired
mocks: IStateGuard (denying fake, one fresh instance per row): evaluate() returns allowed=false with a test-chosen opaque reason and records each (state, event) argument and is wired only to the guard under test for that row; IStateGuard (allowing fake, D8 machine only): evaluate() returns allowed=true and is wired to GuardId::Arm only so the machine can reach ARMED and then FAILSAFE
inputs: D4: DISARMED + ArmRequest; D8: FAILSAFE + RecoveryAccepted; D9: FAULT + ServiceReset
steps: 1. D4: construct a machine, wire denying fake A to GuardId::Arm, dispatch(ResetCompleted), dispatch(InitPassed), then dispatch(ArmRequest) and read the DispatchResult, state(), and fake A's calls | 2. D8: construct a machine, wire the allowing fake to GuardId::Arm and denying fake B to GuardId::Recovery, reach FAILSAFE via ResetCompleted, InitPassed, ArmRequest, CriticalFaultToFailsafe, reset fake B's call record, then dispatch(RecoveryAccepted) and read the results and fake B's calls | 3. D9: construct a machine, wire denying fake C to GuardId::ServiceReset, reach FAULT via ResetCompleted, InitFailed, then dispatch(ServiceReset) and read the results and fake C's calls
expected_result: for every row: outcome RejectedGuardDenied; reason equals the fake's test-chosen reason; state() equals the from state; the row's denying fake recorded exactly one call with (from state, event)
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on outcome, reason, and state() per row; fake call record
notes: FR-067: a denied recovery guard cannot leave FAILSAFE or FAULT. Not asserting DispatchResult.row or to on a guard denial: the design does not define them. Each row has its own fake instance so the one-call assertion is unambiguous.

D9: construct a machine with no guards wired, dispatch(ResetCompleted), dispatch(InitFailed), then dispatch(ServiceReset) and read the DispatchResult and state()
